I'm not an expert, but aren't electronics pretty easy to fuck with? Serious question.
It's not really that simple a question to answer without knowing something about the electronics in question. Different electronics may contain different exploitable points.

I don't mean as far as hacking, I mean interference and disruption type of stuff. Apparently you can even take out the electronics in an entire city and render all the electronics useless. I don't know all that much about it though.

EMP weapons aren't really all that common, but they have existed since the '50s. They come in two varieties, nuclear and non-nuclear. The problem is effective range, and the fact that if you're going to use one you have to get the pulse close enough to the target. This typically means a missile system of some kind which gets expensive.

An NNEMP (non-nuclear Electro-Magnetic Pulse) is not going to fry the electronics in an entire city. A sufficiently large nuclear blast at high altitude would, but really electronic failure is the least of your problems at that point. Weapons designed specifically to generate non-nuclear EMP are not very practical.
Plus military hardware is all shielded against even EMP from nuclear blasts (up to a certain yield, obviously, but still).
With a closed system like this they can be easily and cheaply shielded against interference, even from a nuclear detonation's EMP.

For the amount of control battlefield commanders will want, yes they will be terribly easy to compromise.

On the other hand, if you give the robot inviolable directives while on-base and then send it out, then no one could order it to attack your own troops. The more autonomous the machine, the less susceptible it is to attack. At most, you would want to have an RTB signal you could send out which would get them to call off the attack. The down side is you can't micromanage it and arbitrarily wield it like Thor's Hammer.
